blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entanglement, where heterogeneous information is mixed within coarse-grained memory units; and (2) Organizational Mismatch, where memory structures based primarily on semantic similarity may overlook other associations. To address these challenges, we propose ETAMem, a multi-view memory framework that decouples heterogeneous conversational information and aligns memory representations and organization with its distinct characteristics. Specifically, heterogeneous information parsing extracts atomic memory units and identifies affective information. View-specific memory structuring then organizes these units into three complementary hierarchical views: Event, Affect, and Time. ETAMem incrementally maintains memory structures with adaptively calibrated thresholds. For retrieval, entropy-based retrieval allocates query-specific budgets across views and performs hierarchical search within each view. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S demonstrate that ETAMem outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving relative accuracy improvements of 12.46% and 7.96%, respectively, while maintaining competitive token efficiency. Further analyses demonstrate the complementary benefits of different memory views.
blocks.zh: 长期记忆可以使大语言模型(LLMs)在扩展的对话中保持连贯而个性化的互动. 然而,现有记忆系统面临两大挑战: (1)信息缠绕,在粗糙的内存单元内混杂了各种信息;(2)组织错配,主要基于语义相似的内存结构可能忽略了其他关联. 为了应对这些挑战,我们提议建立ETAMem,这是一个多视角记忆框架,将各种对话信息脱钩,并使记忆表达和组织与它的独特特点相协调。 具体地说,异质信息解析提取出原子内存单位并识别出活性信息. 视图特定内存结构然后将这些单位组织成三个互补的分级视图: 事件,不完美,和时间。 ETAMem递增地维持有适应性校正阈值的内存结构. 对于回取,以Entropy为基础的回取在视图中分配特定查询的预算,并在每个视图中进行分级搜索. information be identified, represented,

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose ETAMem, an E vent- T ime- A ffect Mem ory framework for long-term conversational
agents.
ETAMem first performs heterogeneous information
parsing by decomposing dialogue turns into
semantically complete atomic memory units (AMUs)
and identifying their affective characteristics.
Through view-specific memory structuring,
these AMUs are then organized into three hierarchical views.
Specifically, the Event view organizes factual
experiences through semantic similarity,
the Affect view organizes emotions, attitudes,
and preferences through affect-aware representations,
and the Time view indexes all memories through temporal hierarchies.
To support continual interaction, ETAMem
incrementally maintains the Event and Affect
hierarchies through attachment, splitting, merging,
and lazy summary updates, while adaptively calibrating
maintenance thresholds.
Given a query, entropy-based retrieval
allocates budgets across views
through adaptive routing and performs hierarchical
beam search to retrieve relevant memories.
Experiments on two long-term dialogue memory
benchmarks demonstrate that ETAMem consistently
improves memory performance, particularly on
multi-hop and temporally grounded queries.
Overall, our work makes the following contributions: • We propose ETAMem, a multi-view memory
framework that organizes heterogeneous
conversational information into complementary
Event, Affect, and Time hierarchies with
view-specific representations. • We develop a dynamic memory maintenance
mechanism with adaptive threshold calibration.
We further employ entropy-based routing to
allocate query-specific retrieval budgets
across complementary memory views. • Extensive experiments on LoCoMo and
LongMemEval-S demonstrate that ETAMem outperforms
strong baselines, particularly on multi-hop and
temporal reasoning questions, while maintaining
competitive token costs.

blocks.en: 2.1. Memory Systems for LLM Agents

blocks.en:
Flat memory. Early memory systems store extracted facts or interaction
summaries as independent units, typically retrieved through
semantic similarity ( Zhong et al., 2023 ; Chhikara et al., 2025 ) .
For long-term access, MemGPT ( Packer et al., 2024 ) separates

short-, mid-, and long-term layers, and
LightMem ( Fang et al., 2026 ) uses staged offline consolidation.
These designs emphasize where and when memories are
stored or consolidated, while retrieval often relies
on general semantic matching.

blocks.en: AMU Extraction. ETAMem decomposes each dialogue turn into atomic memory units (AMUs), such that each AMU captures one independent memory item and the resulting set preserves the original information. It then assigns a polarity label to each AMU to distinguish factual content from affective content for subsequent memory organization.

blocks.en: ETAMem maintains its memory trees through online insertion and incremental structural refinement. For each incoming dialogue turn, the extracted AMUs are inserted into their corresponding views. At the end of each session, the Event and Affect views undergo structural maintenance, with Split and Merge operations triggered only when their respective conditions are met. In contrast, the Time view follows a predefined temporal hierarchy and requires only deterministic insertion without maintenance.

blocks.en: 4.3.2. Effect of View-Specific Memory Organization
blocks.zh: 4.3.2. 视图特定记忆组织的效果

blocks.en:
To investigate whether heterogeneous dialogue
information benefits from specialized organization,
we compare ETAMem with three unified strategies
that organize all AMUs into a single hierarchy
without distinguishing information types. Unified Semantic and Unified Affective organize memories
using textual and affective embeddings,
respectively, while Unified Temporal employs a unified
temporal hierarchy.
As shown in Table 5 ,
all unified strategies underperform ETAMem
in overall accuracy.
Unified Semantic performs best among the
unified strategies on LoCoMo, while
Unified Affective achieves the highest
overall accuracy on LongMemEval-S.
Notably, Unified Affective matches ETAMem
on preference-related questions (SSP),
while Unified Temporal matches ETAMem
on temporal reasoning (TR).
These results suggest that different
organizational principles can benefit
specific information types, but no single
unified structure effectively accommodates
their heterogeneous characteristics.
By integrating complementary type-specific
memory views, ETAMem achieves superior
overall performance.

blocks.en: 5. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5.五. 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we proposed ETAMem, a multi-view
memory framework that decouples heterogeneous
conversational information and aligns memory
representations and organization with its
distinct characteristics.
ETAMem integrates heterogeneous information
parsing, view-specific memory structuring,
and entropy-guided retrieval,
supported by dynamic maintenance and adaptive
calibration.
Experiments on two long-term memory benchmarks
demonstrate relative improvements of 12.46% and
7.96% over the strongest baselines, respectively,
with strong multi-hop performance and competitive
token efficiency.
Further analysis highlights the complementary
benefits of different memory views and the
effectiveness of adaptive routing.
Despite these improvements, our affective representations rely on sentiment polarity, which may fail to identify neutral expressions of preferences or attitudes as affective information. Future work will incorporate explicit affective relevance classification to address this limitation.
